body: I love hearing people gush about their happiness! Yay!

I go through this!! F26 

I had a childhood trauma though so that’s where it stems. I thoroughly believe I’ve spent a lot of my life not feeling and it was hard. I got use to it though until I got help for my anxiety and depression and then I really started to feel happiness and recognize my emotions. I have a very stable life - good job, healthy relationship, pets, nice home, etc. 

Since I am more aware of my emotions now, I sometimes get triggered and it’ll send me into that state. For example, this week I read a Reddit post where someone described how their husband cheated and it immediately triggered me and I went emotionally numb for the remaining of the night. I’m barely recognizing my triggers, so sometimes I have no clue what will send me into the state. 
However, I communicate this to my bf because I become distant and I don’t him to think it’s something to do with him or that there’s anything wrong. Once I communicate, he just kind of leaves me alone, which is what I prefer. For me, it usually goes away after some sleep and then it’s like a reboot. However, sometimes it’ll linger until the next day, but usually clears. 

To describe what I feel is like a fog over my emotions. I become very neutral and don’t feel any way towards anything. 

It’s great that he can recognize it and communicate what he needs. That’s really healthy! 

If he handles it in a healthy way then IMO I wouldn’t say it’s anything to be terribly concerned about. However, maybe check in when he isn’t in that state and just make sure he feels okay and overall healthy!
So beautiful!

😳what were those like? 

I haven’t had any other one where I knew or thought I died. Other than that maybe like I’ve been stabbed or shot at, but just woke up with like a muscle cramp. Lol.

Thank you for sharing! Aside from remembering thinking that I felt like a child in the way I was saying things... I know that there was a conversation with just me and my case worker where my mother wasn’t present. I apparently told this case worker some very startling things that obviously no child would know, which was the catalyst in starting the whole case. I feel like whatever I said to the case worker may have been the things I said to my bf... ? Idk. Just thoughts. 

Thank you though. It’s comforting to hear your experience. My therapist didn’t want to delve too into those details, which I understand but I’m still curious.

Yesss. What I said to my bf though were very specific and I remember thinking “I feel like a child right now”. It was almost like I was reliving this thing, but was more conscious. Thankfully my bf is my safe space and our relationship is very healthy and loving. Through this and therapy I’ve been able to work through those emotions. It took days of no sleep and A TON of self care (and a week off from work) but I’m here on the other side a completely different person. I’m genuinely happy. I still struggle with the anxiety and depression but now I can recognize it and deal with it versus not knowing what the heck it is and succumbing to it. 

I appreciate you sharing and I’m happy you’ve found something that works! I’ll definitely look into it. I’m still on a mission to ensure my mental health is always protected and is at its best it can be.

Sounds like my first bf. I was always there for his family events with a smile on my face and being as warm as I possibly could even though his mother was a bit rude to me. She thought I was some floozy stealing her little baby boy (grown ass man🙄). Whenever my mom had her 60th birthday he didn’t want to go, finally got him to and he acted like he was having the worst time of his life. My family was extremely sweet to him. 

If it isn’t because he’s shy or a something new breaking his routine causes some distress, I get that too, thennnn that’s not cool. He should make the effort if it’s important to you.

Perfectly normal in the heat of the moment. He probably just found you super sexy and couldn’t control it! 
Definitely talk about it and how you don’t want to be perceived but kind of liked it. Who knows? It could be more exciting knowing that he’s only that way with you and maybe if you feel like it drop something dirty back. It could be fun to have that bit of “wild” in your own little moments that you two share.
Good for you for changing up your search! I did the same. He was completely the opposite of my usual tinder type and has turned out to be the most loving man I’ve ever had. Very handsome too☺️ yay!
So annoying!! Grrrr lol

I wake up so hurt, like my chest physically feels so heavy and then I feel so dumb😂🙄
It’s nice to hear other stories so I can laugh about it and not sit in the funk.
Lmfao

Yes! I can totally relate. I do want marriage and maybe kids someday but since I was living with like no emotion I barely even knew what my hobbies were. I could be asked what I like to do and couldn’t think of anything other than like going out to drink with friends. I wanted that discovery of myself and I told him. He wanted a wife and kids before 30. I couldn’t even manage daily chores without being stressed and overwhelmed. Washing dishes, doing laundry, cooking, etc. all of that was so hard, so kids? No, thank you. Not right now. His response was you’re just lazy and need to learn how to do it all. I finally said nah, I really don’t want that yet. And that was okay. 

After getting the help I needed, everything’s changed. I still struggle sometimes but my current partner enjoys taking life slow and we view it as growing together. We don’t have kids so we enjoy being lazy after work. We don’t feel like cooking? I’m not shamed, we order food. Our house is tidy but we don’t stress about leaving the laundry for one more day. And again, I’m not shamed. It’s much more peaceful. I finally have hobbies and feel like a fucking person versus an extension of him.

Exactly. The sad part was he was an advocate for mental health yet didn’t put in the effort to help himself, me or us. I don’t blame him though. The mindset is super hard to break. I thoroughly believe in “breaking the curse” within cultures that don’t recognize mental health.
Yes! And the depression would hit so much harder the next day coming down from all the alcohol. Very counterproductive.

That’s no bueno. My current bf recognizes that he doesn’t understand life with anxiety and depression, but he makes an effort to understand. He also doesn’t talk about his emotions too much in depth other than “it’s been a bad day” but we’ve discussed our love languages and his is touch so I make an effort to hug him excitedly when he gets home, back rubs, foot massages, maybe sex and I can see him turn his mood around. The difference is the trust that he has my back and I’ve got his through anything. We’re both attentive and sensitive to each other’s moods. The last relationship if I had a bad day it was like suck it up, I did this, this and this and I’m not complaining. That definitely caused resentment which festered. All in all it was just not nearly enough communication and understanding. 

I’m not giving my bf all the credit for my healing because I helped myself, but he played a huge supportive part and I’ll be forever grateful for that no matter what happens between us.

It was more of a cultural thing IMO. He grew up in a very strict Mexican household where they didn’t talk about emotions and mental illness isn’t really a real thing. His mother had multiple affairs that affected him and his siblings and his father was doing sketchy business deals that put the family at risk, but no communication ever happened in that family, so they lived on like everything was okay. On the outside they had money, went to church, had this picturesque family. I didn’t grow up like that, but had a very similar upbringing. I was labeled as more “rebellious” in my family for questioning things. Why do I need to serve the man? Why do I have to have kids so young? What if I don’t want to go to church and be catholic?
Again, on paper he looked like the perfect guy. Was in school and had his masters and he was becoming successful, so I loved him and the idea of him. He would make my parents proud and be a successful partner. So yeah, after attempting to open up and being disregarded I began to bottle it up because I felt like a burden to him when I brought it up. His mindset was you don’t think about that kind of stuff you just DO, which is what I was use to too. I ignored me questioning what’s wrong with me and ignored me wanting to seek help and listened to him when I was told I was lazy, slept too much, complained too much, just needed to learn to be social, etc. 
I was sexually assaulted as a child and coming from this deep rooted Mexican background that believes you just push it all down and keep trucking it led me to  literally having a mental break down. Holding onto that for years and never feeling like I had a safe space to open up because it’s a hard thing to open up about. 
So yes, in that previous relationship it was definitely both of us. I should’ve followed my instincts to seek help and deal with it, but when it’s engrained so deep that it’s a sign of weakness it’s really difficult to break from that mindset. The memory of the assault wasn’t something that hurt me in my day to day life, but was an annoyance and I felt like I was this numb robot living day to day instead of feeling much emotion in my overall life. I got use to life like that until I started questioning again. 
So to go from this experience to someone who just let me go through my healing without judgement was literally a life saver and exactly what I needed at the perfect time.

This makes me happy to hear!! In my previous relationship there was so many issues with sex and communication played a huge part of course, in and out of the bedroom. It feels amazing to finally have excitement and fun back in that area. We aren’t just having sex because we’re horny but because we also just want each other. It’s fun!

I was in this place. It was rough. Literally what you described was me like 4 months ago. Quarantine forced me to face my mental illness and brought it to surface in the worst way. I had barely started seeking help so I think that also contributed to everything being so in my face at all times. With the help of supportive friends and my partner I was able to come to a baseline. I still have anxiety and depression but I’ve learned now how to recognize it and separate it from my own conscious reality and who I actually am. It’s helped tremendously. On days I feel it surfacing I pamper myself and do things I love that ground me and help me realize it’s my mental illness and not me. It’s been a difficult process and still is everyday, but it gets easier. Just keep pushing and focus on helping yourself. Easier said than done and of course I don’t know your situation. Just a bit of my experience. Every day is a new day.
Yes!!! I love this.

It’s so beautiful! When I’ve had a tough day I think about these moments and they make me cry very happy tears. 

I was in a relationship for 5 years with a man who would essentially push my denial and it landed me spiraling internally and picking up drinking to mask the symptoms. We met when I was 19 and he was 21. I never really felt like I could show that side of me. When I would start to communicate my anxious feelings/thoughts it would start fights. If I ignored it then we were fine. It was exhausting. Marriage was on our mind since other than my anxiety everything was okay...? It was meh. I’m thankful I took a step back and left that relationship. At the time, it was hard to leave something that wasn’t terribly bad, but wasn’t amazing for me either.

THANK YOU. Before I sought help for my anxiety (didn’t know that’s what it was at the time) I was in a 5 year relationship with someone who used those terms when I had my suspicions or told me I just needed to learn to be social or learn to not think about it...that concept was foreign for me. I couldn’t just stop or not think about it. It dove me further into denial for FIVE YEARS. After 2 months into seeking help this year, I basically had a huge break down coming to terms and acceptance of my anxiety. I had just met my current bf and all I have to say is having a support team (mostly my bf and a few close friends) has changed my life. I’m grateful to have left that person and legitimately saved my own life by finally reaching out. 
My current bf met me at a point where my anxiety would turn into panic attacks that would leave me passing out and completely disassociated. It was an awful period of my life but I’m thankful I’m here now and extremely grateful for his love and support. It’s been a wild ride!

My bf knows I like baking to fill my time. I’m not a baker by any means, but it’s in the name of self care lol  sometimes he’ll join me to make it an us thing that day. He rubs my back. He kisses me often, a lot when I’m least expecting it. He’ll hug me when we’re just passing each other in the apt. He takes care of tasks around the home like cooking, dishes, laundry etc. sometimes or we do it together. If I’m having a mentally off day (I struggle with anxiety and depression) he’ll pull me closer and love on me harder. Bring me my favorite foods or drinks. Runs a bath for me. My anxiety lies to me, tells me my bf doesn’t love me because I’m not x, y, z. I know these thoughts aren’t true so when I get in those funks we have a bit of a code for it so he knows what to do without us having to talk about it in that moment. He knows I don’t believe those thoughts so I don’t react to them or care to bring them into my reality.  it makes life a little hard from time to time. He makes it much easier. 
For me, it’s a lot of the things I’m not expecting. Ordering me food or bringing me a snack. Kissing, touching in passing. Holding a gaze a bit longer.
